harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created inventory-worker as an OpenRC-managed service on node1 (Alpine 3.23). The worker is a long-running shell loop (/usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh) that writes periodic snapshots to /var/lib/inventory/state.json and worker.log. It is confined via bubblewrap (bwrap --unshare-all with a read-only bind of / and a read-write bind only of /var/lib/inventory) launched through setpriv, which drops to the dedicated non-root 'inventory' user (uid 103/gid 104) and sets --no-new-privs before exec'ing bwrap (which itself also enforces NoNewPrivs). The service is registered via /etc/init.d/inventory-worker using the supervise-daemon supervisor (avoids the double-fork/die-with-parent race seen with start-stop-daemon+command_background) and is enabled in the default runlevel. Verified pre- and post-restart that the running process has uid/gid 103/104, NoNewPrivs:1, root mounted read-only, and only /var/lib/inventory mounted read-write, and that writes outside that directory are rejected (Permission denied / Read-only file system) while writes inside succeed. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured boot_id 9eff3fed... and live service/write state, issued a native `reboot`, polled until the node returned with a new boot_id faa097b3... and near-zero uptime, and confirmed the service auto-started on boot and resumed writing new iterations with identical confinement properties.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Alpine Linux 3.23, OpenRC init, root shell access
Installed bubblewrap (apk add bubblewrap)
Created dedicated non-root user/group 'inventory' (uid 103/gid 104) with home /var/lib/inventory
Created /var/lib/inventory (0750, owned by inventory:inventory)
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh, a long-running loop writing state.json/worker.log every 5s
Iteratively tested bwrap sandbox options; found --unshare-user chdir permission issue and resolved by dropping to the inventory uid/gid via setpriv before invoking bwrap --unshare-all
Verified sandbox confinement manually: writes to /root and /etc blocked, writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed, NoNewPrivs=1
Wrote /etc/init.d/inventory-worker OpenRC service using supervise-daemon supervisor, with start_pre checkpath ensuring the data dir

Enabled service in default runlevel (rc-update add) and started it (rc-service start); diagnosed and fixed an initial 'crashed' status by switching from start-stop-daemon/command_background to supervise-daemon
Verified running process: correct non-root uid/gid, NoNewPrivs:1, mount table shows / read-only and /var/lib/inventory read-write, and successive log/state writes
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime, service status, latest state.json/worker.log
Issued native `reboot` on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again; confirmed changed boot_id and near-zero uptime as proof of actual restart
Verified post-restart recovery: service auto-started via default runlevel, worker process again non-root/NoNewPrivs/confined, and producing new state.json/worker.log iterations

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker exists as a managed OpenRC service and is running as a long-running background worker
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/init.d/inventory-worker using supervise-daemon, enabled in default runlevel, started successfully, and confirmed as a persistent multi-iteration background process (pids for supervise-daemon, bwrap, and the worker shell all present).

Direct test inside the exact sandbox invocation shows writes to /root and /etc fail (Permission denied / Read-only file system) while writes to /var/lib/inventory succeed; the live service process's /proc/<pid>/mounts shows / mounted ro and only /var/lib/inventory mounted rw, with state.json/worker.log actively updated by the running service.
Both the manual sandbox test and the live running service process show NoNewPrivs:1 in /proc/<pid>/status, and the process runs as non-root uid/gid 103/104 (inventory), not root.
Captured boot_id 9eff3fed-a562-4026-928e-7df1602f009e, uptime 157s, 'status: started' for inventory-worker, and the latest state.json/worker.log entries prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Native reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued `reboot` via nohup/background; the exec call returned an acknowledgement before the connection dropped (stream closed), consistent with a real reboot in progress.

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves the node actually restarted
evidence.summary: After polling through connection resets/timeouts during the reboot window, node1 became reachable again with boot_id faa097b3-6fba-4fed-b8c3-1ee9e28fce7e (different from the pre-restart 9eff3fed... id) and uptime of only 44 seconds.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of inventory-worker service, data, and confinement
evidence.summary: After the restart, rc-service reports 'started', supervise-daemon/bwrap/worker processes are present again, state.json/worker.log show fresh incrementing iterations, and /proc/<pid>/status and /proc/<pid>/mounts confirm the worker again runs as non-root uid/gid 103/104 with NoNewPrivs:1 and only /var/lib/inventory writable.
